name: Calendar Seasonality
rationale: Calendar rules test whether recurring date-based effects survive realistic costs and validation.
expected_benefit: Potential return concentration with lower market exposure.
failure_modes: Data-mined calendar effects that vanish out of sample.
Too few observations for reliable inference.
Rules that look good only in one market regime.

canonical_variants.name: Turn-of-month equity exposure
canonical_variants.description: Hold the market only around the turn of each month.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A turn-of-month exposure rule may retain meaningful equity returns while reducing time in market.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Retain at least 50% of benchmark CAGR with materially lower exposure.

canonical_variants.name: Sell-in-May seasonal filter
canonical_variants.description: Hold equities during historically stronger months and cash during historically weaker months.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A prespecified seasonal equity filter may reduce drawdown without giving up too much long-term growth.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 20% relative while retaining at least 70% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Weekday reversal
canonical_variants.description: Test one prespecified weekday entry/exit pattern.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A single prespecified weekday reversal rule may improve returns relative to time in market.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe after realistic costs and remain stable across decades.

suggested_validation: Require a long sample because signals are sparse.
Do not search many date windows.
Use train/test by calendar era, not random splits.
references: Academic literature on turn-of-month and seasonality effects
execution_notes: The current strategy schema does not support date/calendar conditions.
